thesis: Nu Holdings Ltd. (ticker **NU**) is a Cayman holding company for a digital money platform operating mainly in **Brazil, Mexico, and Colombia**. **[Fact]** As of December 31, 2025 it served **131 million** customers with credit and prepaid cards, demand deposits and Money Boxes, Pix payments, personal and SME loans, investments, and insurance distribution. **[Fact]** FY2025 total revenue was **US$15.8 billion** (+37%) and net income attributable to the parent was **US$2.87 billion** (+45%). **[Fact]** Customers fund the balance sheet with **US$41.9 billion** of deposits, mostly payable on demand, while an interest-earning credit book and card receivables drive net interest and fee income. Nu presents results in U.S. dollars under IFRS and files a Form 20-F.
why_market_wrong: **[Inference]** At about **US$14.68** per share, the market may treat Nu as a generic high-growth fintech priced for perfect credit outcomes, or conversely as a bank forever capped by Brazil rates, without separating the **deposit franchise** (hard to copy) from **credit origination** (increasingly contested by Mercado Pago and, later, Sea Monee). **[Inference]** Unit economics in the FY2025 20-F (ARPAC **US$13.3**, cost to serve **US$0.8**, Brazil funding near **81% of CDI**) support a durable compounding engine even if credit growth cools from last year’s pace. **[Inference]** US national-bank optionality (OCC preliminary conditional approval January 2026) is easy to overpay for and easy to ignore; we leave it mostly outside base owner cash.
